title: Test authoring record
description: What tests were written for one task, what each proves, and what was deliberately left untested. `fails_when` is required on every test because a test that cannot be said to fail for a stated reason is a test nobody can evaluate — and a vacuous assertion is worse than a missing one, since it occupies the place the real test would go. `not_applicable` carries the edge cases considered and dismissed, with why: an edge case dismissed silently is indistinguishable from one nobody thought of. The producer does not run what it writes, so nothing here records a result.

record_id.description: Supplied by the caller and never minted by the producer.

implementation_record_id.description: The implementation these tests were written against. Required because its inferences are what the tests must pin: a decision nobody specified stays incidental until a test states it.

kind.description: What the task was, which decides what must exist afterwards. `restructure` requires no new behavioral test — tests written alongside a restructuring describe the arrangement just made and pass by construction.

proves.description: The criterion or the inference this test binds.

fails_when.description: The change to the implementation that would make this test fail. A test with no such change proves nothing.

why.description: Why it does not apply. Asserting a guarantee nobody made is a reason not to test something.

untested.description: What remains unproven and why, including a restructured area the existing tests do not cover — which is a finding rather than a reason to write tests describing the new shape.

contested.description: Where the author believes the implementation is wrong. The test states what the criterion requires; the disagreement is recorded here rather than resolved by changing the implementation or by writing the test to pass.
